# v0.49.31

This patch fixes four Oh My Pi and Pi problems from one detailed report, stops an OpenCode 2 `/goal` compaction from pushing every request past the context window, lets very large Pi sessions run without refusals, shortens how long Pi holds the database lock when queued drops land, and makes the dreamer's verify and memory-mapping tasks stop failing on valid answers.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode or Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Every Oh My Pi turn refused after local midnight (#820, thanks @TheOrdinaryWow):** Oh My Pi adds a date and folder reminder row to the request after Magic Context has checked the turn's structure, and the check didn't expect it. From midnight on, every turn was refused until Oh My Pi restarted. The check now accepts that reminder only when it matches Oh My Pi's exact template, with a valid date and the session's own folder, in the position Oh My Pi uses. Any other extra row is still refused.
- **Oh My Pi Responses turns refused after a matching tag (#821, thanks @TheOrdinaryWow):** when the tag Magic Context re-applies equals the one the model echoed, the reply was prepared without its phase, so every later turn was refused. The phase is now kept in that case.
- **Pi's local embedding preflight never ran (#822, thanks @TheOrdinaryWow):** an early return skipped the pooling check, so session backfill retried every minute and never finished. The check now runs.
- **A Pi log line printed `[object Object]` (#823, thanks @TheOrdinaryWow):** the historian's fallback models now print by name.
- **OpenCode 2 `/goal` could push every request past the context window (#824, thanks @elmagow):** when OpenCode 2 compacts a long session, it adds a "recent context" block of raw conversation to its checkpoint, and in an agent session that block could reach millions of tokens. It was then sent on every request, and reverting didn't remove it. Magic Context already serves those messages itself, so on OpenCode 2.1 and newer its compaction answer now asks for no recent-context block. Sessions already affected, and OpenCode 2.0, have the block trimmed before the request is sent, and every request carrying a checkpoint is measured against the window first. No message that wasn't summarized yet is lost.
- **Very large Pi sessions were refused:** Pi sessions with around 200,000 or more tags could be refused, because a memory estimate counted far more than the session uses and tagging took too long. Sessions up to 250,000 tags now run, and the requests sent are unchanged.
- **Pi held the database lock for seconds when queued drops landed:** applying a large batch of queued drops rewrote a stored record once per drop while holding the shared database's write lock, up to about 10 seconds. It is now written once per batch, and the lock is held for a fraction of a second.
- **Pi's retrospective read reminder notices as if the user had written them:** it now strips them, as OpenCode already did.
- **Dreamer verify ignored `timeout_minutes`:** verify and verify-broad cut every batch at 4 minutes, whatever the configured task timeout, so slow models never finished a batch. They now keep starting batches until the configured deadline, and each batch can use the time left.
- **Dreamer memory mapping treated a valid empty answer as a failure:** when a model correctly left every memory in a batch unmapped, as the prompt allows, the answer was rejected and every fallback model was tried in turn. A well-formed empty answer now counts as a completed batch, and those memories retry later on their usual backoff. Malformed answers still fall back.

# v0.49.30

This patch fixes a Pi session stalling on replies its model wrote as blank drop markers, cuts main-thread CPU on long OpenCode 2 sessions, repairs `doctor repair-db`, and adds logging for hidden historian sessions on OpenCode 2.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode or Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Replies written as `[dropped ]` stalled a session (#815, thanks @tevenfeng):** Magic Context removes assistant replies that contain nothing but drop markers, so the model doesn't copy them and stop. It recognized `[dropped]` and `[dropped N]`, but not the blank form `[dropped ]` some models write. Those replies stayed in history and the model kept stopping. All three forms are now removed, with one rule shared by OpenCode and Pi. The removal still happens only on a pass that rebuilds the prompt anyway, so it costs no extra cache write.
- **Main-thread CPU on long OpenCode 2 sessions (#817, thanks @iceteaSA):**
  - **The sidebar usage query:** it read every message of the session on each sidebar poll. It now uses the session index. On the reporter's long sessions, one poll took about 19 ms before and well under a millisecond after.
  - **Message times:** every pass re-read the creation and completion times of every message, although a finished message's times never change. Times are now reused for user messages and finished replies, and re-read only when OpenCode changes or rewrites a message. The times shown to the model are byte-identical.
  - **The history boundary check:** a per-pass check read full summary rows when it needs only two fields. It now reads just those fields.
- **`doctor repair-db` could not salvage a damaged database:** its recovery replay failed on every SQLite version, because the shell's defensive mode blocks the schema writes that recovery needs. Recovery now turns defensive mode off on the fresh replay database only. Every row comes back, along with statistics and search-index definitions. The backup before repair and the integrity checks are unchanged.

## Diagnostics

- **Hidden historian sessions on OpenCode 2 (#818, thanks @Ven0maus):** Magic Context now logs when it creates each hidden historian or dreamer session, and whether it keeps or removes it afterwards. The log also records the `keep_subagents` value in effect at startup. These lines help find why some users see a "session not found" message on OpenCode 2.2.

releases.name: Dashboard dashboard-v0.20.22
releases.body:
## Fixes

- **Memories tab:** category headers now show each project's real memory counts. Before, they counted only the first 200 memories loaded. Every memory can now be reached by paging, and a list that's cut short says how many are shown out of the total.
- **Memory mural:** the mural image now displays. Before, the box stayed blank even after the mural rendered.

# v0.49.29

This patch fixes console windows flashing on Windows, OpenCode 2 sessions showing zero tokens, a small config mistake that silently turned memory off, and two cases where Magic Context could change bytes already sent to the model.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode or Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Console windows flashing on Windows (#804, #553, thanks @butterbrodskiy and @devsiac):** the dreamer's verify step ran its git commands without hiding their window, so one verify pass could flash dozens of PowerShell or CMD windows and steal focus. Those commands now run hidden. A test now checks every place Magic Context starts a process, including the ones run through promisified helpers.
- **"Total tokens 0" in the OpenCode 2 sidebar (#805, thanks @maxbrunet):** the sidebar read token totals from OpenCode 1's message table, which is empty on OpenCode 2. It now reads OpenCode 2's own messages.
- **OpenCode 2 dreamer tasks recording zero tokens (#810, thanks @iceteaSA):** on OpenCode 2, the dreamer's tool-using tasks (memory mapping, verify, curate, retrospective) and smart-note evaluation recorded no token usage. They now record the usage their completions report. A memory-mapping batch that times out now keeps the mappings it already produced, instead of reading an empty transcript and losing them.
- **A small config mistake silently turned memory off (#811, thanks @Drynwhyl):** an invalid value anywhere under `memory`, such as an out-of-range `injection_budget_tokens`, marked the whole config untrusted, which turns memory off for a project at its first start. The memory tool then only said "disabled for this project".
  - **What happens now:** an invalid value falls back to its default with a warning, and memory stays on. Only fields that decide which embeddings and which project a memory belongs to (the embedding provider, model and endpoint, the local runtime, the memory switches, home-project admission) still mark the config untrusted, because a wrong value there could delete stored embeddings.
  - **An invalid `git_commit_indexing.max_commits`:** commit indexing keeps working, but deleting old commits pauses until the value is fixed.
  - **When memory is off for this reason:** the memory tool now names the invalid fields.
- **A busy-database fallback could erase a served reminder:** when the database is busy, Magic Context serves its last good request again. Applying newly committed drops to that request also erased reminder text already served on a dropped message, so the request changed and the provider cache rebuilt. Reminders already served now stay until a permitted rebuild. Normal passes still render every drop as the plain placeholder.
- **OpenCode 2.2.0 instruction updates:** OpenCode 2.2.0 lets plugins post instruction updates mid-conversation as system rows.
  - **The summarizer** no longer reads those rows as something you said.
  - **The busy-database fallback** now works in sessions that contain them. An update that arrives right after such a fallback is no longer dropped, and an instruction edited after OpenCode's checkpoint now makes the fallback refuse instead of sending the old text.

# v0.49.28

This patch fixes two dreamer problems: memory mapping falling behind in large projects, and Pi dreamer tasks stopping at 30 minutes regardless of their configured timeout.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode or Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Memory mapping falling behind (#809, thanks @iceteaSA):** the dreamer maps memories to source files in batches of five, each given a fixed four-minute slice. In projects where a batch regularly needs close to four minutes, two timed-out batches in a row stopped the night's run, so only a few memories were mapped each night and the backlog kept growing.
  - **What happens now:** a timed-out batch is split into smaller batches (five becomes two, two and one), and those run straight away in the same run. Mappings a timed-out batch already saved are kept, and only the rest are retried.
  - **When a run still stops:** only after a single memory times out twice in a row with nothing saved.
  - **Settings:** none added. The per-batch slice and the task timeout are unchanged.
  - **Hosts:** OpenCode and Pi.
- **Pi dreamer tasks stopping at 30 minutes (#784, PR #808, thanks @izhangzhihao and @mvanhorn):** on Pi and Oh My Pi, each dreamer task runs in a child process that was always stopped after 30 minutes, so a task configured with a longer `timeout_minutes` was cut off early. The child process now gets the task's own timeout plus five minutes, so the dreamer's timeout always decides and reports the right reason. The user-memory review task now uses its own configured timeout too.
